terms.name: Accessible name
terms.definition: The string assistive technology announces for a control, computed from label, aria-labelledby, aria-label, or its own content in a fixed order of precedence.

terms.name: Alt text
terms.definition: The text alternative that stands in for an image, written to serve the same purpose in the same context rather than to describe every detail.

terms.name: Ascender
terms.definition: The part of a lowercase letter such as b, d, or h that rises above the x-height.

terms.name: Baseline
terms.definition: The invisible line that most letters sit on, and the line every other vertical type metric is measured from.

terms.name: Broken grid
terms.definition: A composition that sets up a grid and then deliberately violates it, overlapping and offsetting elements to create tension.

terms.name: Card flip
terms.definition: Rotating a card about its own axis to show a second face on the back, with the hidden face pre-rotated and its backface hidden so only one side is ever visible.

terms.name: Check answers
terms.definition: A review screen listing everything the reader entered, with a change link beside each answer, shown before the submission is final.

terms.name: Color banding
terms.definition: The visible stripes that appear across a gradient when a display or file cannot render enough intermediate steps to keep the transition smooth.

terms.name: color-mix()
terms.definition: A CSS function that blends two colours by a chosen percentage in a chosen colour space, so hover and disabled variants are derived rather than hand-picked.

terms.name: Conformance level
terms.definition: The A, AA, or AAA tier a WCAG success criterion sits in, and the tier a product claims, which is what people mean when they say a design is AA.

terms.name: Corner radius
terms.definition: How far a shape's corners are rounded off, measured as the radius of the circle that replaces the square angle, and the one number that decides how soft a UI reads.

terms.name: Data grid
terms.definition: A spreadsheet-like table where individual cells take focus and can be edited, navigated cell by cell with the arrow keys.

terms.name: Did you mean
terms.definition: Offering a corrected spelling for a query that returned little or nothing, either as a suggestion to accept or as a substitution the reader can undo.

terms.name: Dolly and zoom
terms.definition: Borrowing the camera's vocabulary: dolly moves the viewer through the scene, zoom scales the scene itself, and the interface reads as travelling rather than rearranging.

terms.name: Dropdown
terms.definition: The loose everyday word for any panel that opens downward from a trigger, whatever the panel holds and whatever the trigger does with it.

terms.name: Emoji picker
terms.definition: A searchable grid of emoji organised by category, with recent choices remembered and skin tone chosen once.

terms.name: Eyedropper
terms.definition: A tool that turns the cursor into a sampler so a colour can be picked from anywhere on screen, usually with a magnified preview of the pixel under it.

terms.name: Figure
terms.definition: An image, table or code block bound to its caption so the two travel together and can be referred to from the running text.

terms.name: Floating action button
terms.definition: A round, raised button that hovers above the content in a fixed corner, carrying the one action the screen is most for.

terms.name: Focusable scroll region
terms.definition: Giving a scrollable box its own tab stop so a keyboard user can scroll it, which matters whenever the content inside holds no focusable element of its own.

terms.name: Frutiger Aero
terms.definition: The mid 2000s look of glossy gradients, bubbles, water, bright skies, and clean humanist type, named after the typeface and Windows Aero.

terms.name: Grade
terms.definition: A variable font axis that thickens or thins strokes without changing any character's width, so text can get darker without reflowing.

terms.name: Has popup
terms.definition: A hint on a trigger that says something will open and what kind of thing it will be, a menu, a listbox, a dialog, before the reader commits to pressing it.

terms.name: Honeypot field
terms.definition: A form field hidden from people but visible to automated form fillers, used to reject submissions that fill it in without challenging anyone.

terms.name: Image
terms.definition: An embedded picture, sized and cropped by the layout around it, carrying the alternative text that stands in when it cannot be seen.

terms.name: Interactive transition
terms.definition: A transition whose progress is held by an ongoing gesture, so the reader can drag it partway, hesitate, and either complete it or send it back.

terms.name: Kawaii UI
terms.definition: A cute style of pastel fills, rounded everything, oversized eyes and blush marks, sticker and mascot characters, and hand-lettered or bubbly rounded type.

terms.name: Large text threshold
terms.definition: The size at which text counts as large for contrast purposes (about 18pt, or 14pt when bold) and its required ratio drops from 4.5:1 to 3:1.

terms.name: Lightbox
terms.definition: An overlay that shows one image or video large over a dimmed page, with next and previous controls and a dismiss.

terms.name: Logo cloud
terms.definition: A row or grid of customer logos used as social proof, usually flattened to one colour so no brand dominates.

terms.name: Maximalism
terms.definition: A style that fills the screen on purpose with layered color, pattern, and type, treating abundance rather than restraint as the message.

terms.name: Mid-century modern
terms.definition: A 1950s and 60s style of muted mustard, teal, and burnt orange, tapered organic shapes, textured paper grounds, and friendly geometric sans type.

terms.name: Morph transition
terms.definition: A transition where a shape or icon is interpolated into a different shape rather than swapped, so the two states read as one object changing.

terms.name: Natural language interface
terms.definition: An interface whose input is ordinary language, typed or spoken: the user states an intent in their own words and the system parses it, instead of picking from controls.

terms.name: Object fit
terms.definition: How a picture or video is resized inside a box whose shape it does not match: stretched to fill, letterboxed to fit whole, or cropped to cover every edge.

terms.name: Orbit
terms.definition: Rotating a camera around a fixed point by dragging, so the scene appears to turn while the subject stays centred.

terms.name: Page header
terms.definition: The band at the top of a screen carrying the page title, its context, and the actions that apply to the page as a whole.

terms.name: Permission priming
terms.definition: Explaining why access is needed in the product's own dialog first, and only firing the operating system prompt once the reader has said yes to that.

terms.name: Popconfirm
terms.definition: A small confirmation bubble anchored to the control you just pressed, asking whether you meant it without opening a dialog over the page.

terms.name: Progress bar
terms.definition: A filling bar reporting how far along a task is, determinate when the end is known and indeterminate when it is not.

terms.name: Quasimode
terms.definition: A temporary mode held open by the user, such as a key kept down, so it cannot be forgotten and ends the moment the hold ends.

terms.name: Reading flow
terms.definition: A CSS property that repoints reading and tab order at the visual arrangement of a flex or grid container, instead of leaving both stuck in source order.

terms.name: Retro-futurism
terms.definition: A style that pictures the future the way an earlier decade pictured it, so the technology shown is advanced but the type, color, and hardware belong to the past.

terms.name: Runt
terms.definition: A single word left alone on the last line of a paragraph or heading.

terms.name: Scroll lock
terms.definition: Freezing the page behind an open overlay so a wheel or swipe moves the overlay's own content and never the document underneath.

terms.name: Selection color
terms.definition: The highlight painted behind text a reader has selected, which a page can restyle and thereby break the contrast the operating system had guaranteed.

terms.name: Sidebar
terms.definition: A persistent vertical region alongside the main content holding navigation or secondary controls, often collapsible on narrow screens.

terms.name: Smart defaults
terms.definition: Prefilling a choice with the answer most people in this situation want, so the common case needs no work and every other case is still reachable.

terms.name: Spatial UI
terms.definition: Interface designed to sit in three dimensional space, where panels are made of a system glass material and hierarchy is carried by depth rather than by colour.

terms.name: Stacking context
terms.definition: A self contained depth ordering created by certain properties, inside which z-index only competes locally and can never escape to the level above.

terms.name: Streak
terms.definition: A count of consecutive periods in which the reader did the thing, displayed prominently and lost if a period is missed.

terms.name: Swipe deck
terms.definition: A stack of cards judged one at a time, each thrown left or right to record a binary decision and reveal the next card underneath.

terms.name: Tap
terms.definition: A single press and lift of one finger on a touch surface, the touch equivalent of a click, used to activate a control or select an item.

terms.name: Time zone display
terms.definition: Whose clock a time is shown on, the reader's or the event's, and saying which, because a time with no zone beside it is a meeting somebody is going to miss.

terms.name: Touch target size
terms.definition: The minimum area a control must offer a finger or imprecise pointer, measured on the activation region rather than the painted glyph.

terms.name: Type to confirm
terms.definition: Guarding a destructive action by making the reader type the name of the thing being destroyed before the confirm button becomes usable.

terms.name: Velocity skew
terms.definition: Skewing or stretching content in proportion to how fast the page is scrolling and easing it back to square when the scroll stops, so speed shows up in the shape of the content.

terms.name: Web font
terms.definition: A font file downloaded by the page rather than taken from the reader's device, declared in CSS and delivered like any other asset.

terms.name: Z pattern
terms.definition: The scanning shape on sparse pages: across the top, diagonally down to the lower left, then across the bottom to the final call to action.
